1) Can you confirm whether the data Redwood would access/receive includes PHI (e.g., patient identifiers, clinical notes)?
2) Which hosting environment is in-scope for the integration (Acme AWS account us-east-1, Acme on-prem, or a managed environment)?
3) Retention / logging requirements: any legal retention windows beyond standard 90-day logs? You mentioned 7 years for some records on the call — can you confirm which datasets require that retention?
4) Do you have any specific encryption-at-rest or HSM/KMS requirements we should be aware of?

If you prefer, we can capture these in a short intake form during the kickoff. Also proposing to add Rishi Malhotra (CS) to the kickoff so we can discuss SLA and runbook expectations.

Neha / Marissa —

Answers below to your questions: 

1) PHI: yes, the integration will include PHI. Systems in scope:
   - Epic EHR (patient demographics, encounters, limited clinical notes)
   - Snowflake analytics warehouse (anonymized + some keyed PHI for matching)
   - Customer portal (React app) that surfaces appointments/notifications (no full PHI in UI but identifiers present)

2) Hosting: primary deployment is in our AWS account (us-east-1). We do have a subset of systems on-prem but the initial integration will be AWS.

3) Retention: legal requires 7-year retention for certain clinical records. For logs and request traces we prefer 90 days but can coordinate specific retention for PHI-related artifacts.

4) Encryption: we use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys for sensitive datasets; we will expect TLS in transit and strong encryption at rest.

Kickoff timing: Tue Oct 27, 10:30-11:15 AM PST works for our group — suggested attendees: Luke (InfoSec), Samira (Product), Procurement rep, Mark (CFO, brief intro), plus Neha / Rishi / Marissa from Redwood. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
